content.question: Why is Newton's method rarely used in practice for large models?
options: It converges too slowly to be useful.
It cannot minimize non-convex loss functions.
Computing and inverting the Hessian is computationally expensive and requires a lot of resources.
It stops working when the gradient becomes very small.
content.answer: Computing and inverting the Hessian is computationally expensive and requires a lot of resources.
